requirements: R1: can_view returns True only when both tenant identifiers are present and exactly equal
R2: can_view returns False for different tenants and for any missing identifier
risks: auth.can_view (authorization decision): critical — an over-permissive result exposes another tenant's data
invariants: I1: no resource is readable across tenant boundaries

criteria.evidence: auth.py:2 `bool(user_tenant and resource_tenant)` checks presence only, never equality
cross-tenant access allowed: can_view("tenant-a","tenant-b") -> True; missing identifiers are denied

findings.claim: can_view never compares the two tenant identifiers, so any user with a tenant can view any other tenant's resource; the test suite cannot fail on this because it has no cross-tenant case. (merged from regression-1, security-1, tests-1: same root cause; and acceptance-2, regression-2, security-2: absent cross-tenant test while the requirement is broken — evidence kept, merged per adjudication gate step 6)
evidence: auth.py:2 `return bool(user_tenant and resource_tenant)` — no equality check
no test with two different present tenants
findings.failure_mechanism: can_view("tenant-a", "tenant-b") -> both truthy -> True -> tenant-a reads tenant-b's resources; suite passes. Suggested check: assertFalse(can_view("tenant-a", "tenant-b")) — fails against auth.py:2.

findings.claim: Missing-identifier denial tested only for user_tenant=None (missing resource tenant, both missing, empty strings untested).
evidence: auth.py:2 `bool(a and b)` returns False for None or '' in either position
findings.failure_mechanism: a future refactor could special-case only the tested None-user path while leaving other missing-identifier combinations unhandled; suite would stay green
findings.rejection_reason: test-strength on correct code: auth.py:2 `bool(a and b)` returns False for None or "" in either position; no test named in required evidence.

minimum_next_action: Return user_tenant == resource_tenant only when both are present (e.g. `bool(user_tenant) and user_tenant == resource_tenant`) and add a cross-tenant denial test.
